# vcell-chombo builds on Windows with clang-cl and flang, not MSVC and not
# MinGW. This follows vcell-fvsolver, which builds 167 fixed-form Fortran files,
# C++ and a pybind11 wheel that way; its Windows-AMD64_profile.txt is the model
# for this one.
#
# Why not MSVC: it has no Fortran compiler at all, and roughly half of Chombo is
# Fortran generated by a perl preprocessor. vcell-hy3s answers that with Intel's
# ifx driving MSVC, but it can: that code was originally written for MSVC and
# Intel, and Chombo's makefiles carry no toolchain block for ifx.
#
# Why not MinGW, which was tried first and got the whole dependency tree built:
# CPython's Windows builds are MSVC/UCRT, so a MinGW extension module would be
# off the supported path for the pybind11 wheel this repo is eventually meant to
# grow -- and pyvcell already pulls pyvcell-fvsolver, pyvcell-mbsolver, numpy
# and h5py into one interpreter, which is where that would be felt. clang-cl
# produces MSVC-ABI binaries and keeps the Fortran.
#
# MSYS2 is still part of the build and is not a leftover of that attempt.
# ChomboFortran is perl, and chombo/lib/mk needs GNU make and a shell with
# pipefail whoever compiles the code. It is a build tool here; nothing it ships
# compiles anything.

[settings]
arch=x86_64
build_type=Release
compiler=clang
# 22 rather than fvsolver's 21, and forced rather than preferred: flang is not
# in LLVM 21's official Windows installer at all. Windows flang starts at 22.
#
# This has to match the LLVM the workflow installs. Conan will not catch a
# mismatch -- it never compares this against the compiler it runs, it only
# hashes it into package IDs -- so .github/workflows/windows.yml checks it
# explicitly, and the two have to move together.
compiler.version=22
# vcell-expressionparser and vcell-messaging use std::format, so conanfile.py's
# check_min_cppstd rejects anything below 20. fvsolver's profile says 17 because
# fvsolver has no such submodule requirement.
compiler.cppstd=20
# Static, so win64.zip carries the executables and no MSVC runtime redistributable,
# which matches what the solver release contract wants from an archive.
#
# Worth revisiting when the wheel lands rather than assuming it carries over:
# CPython is built /MD, and a /MT extension module beside it is the classic
# heap-mismatch hazard if allocations cross the boundary. fvsolver ships wheels
# from a static profile, so there is a precedent to check against rather than a
# known answer.
compiler.runtime=static
compiler.runtime_version=v144
os=Windows

[conf]
# Required, not a preference: conanfile.py's layout() only flattens the tree to
# build/generators when this is set. Without it cmake_layout() emits
# build/Release/generators and the workflow's paths miss.
tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:generator=Ninja

# Conan generates config files for its dependencies; prefer those over CMake's
# bundled Find modules, which is what finds HDF5 and libzip here. Taken from
# fvsolver's profile, where it is load-bearing for the same reason.
tools.cmake.cmaketoolchain:extra_variables={"CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_PREFER_CONFIG": "ON"}

# The dependency sources are not ours and their warnings are not actionable
# here; the solver's own translation units are compiled by CMake and unaffected.
tools.build:cflags=["-w"]
tools.build:cxxflags=["-w"]

[buildenv]
# clang-cl for the C/C++ halves, so the objects are MSVC-ABI. flang for Fortran.
# CMake is told the same thing explicitly in the workflow, because Chombo's own
# makefiles read $(CXX) and $(FC) and have to agree with what CMake resolved.
CC=clang-cl
CXX=clang-cl
FC=flang

[options]
fPIC=True
shared=False
# No broker to report to on the desktop local-run path, and conanfile.py drops
# the libcurl requirement on Windows regardless.
include_messaging=False
